title: Update Usage & Billing FAQ: billed tokens, caching, retries, and dispute process
author: Elliot Price
description:
Summary: This PR refreshes the public-ish Usage & Billing FAQ to align with current platform behavior and the ongoing metering hardening work. Primary goals are (a) reduce invoice disputes by being explicit about definitions (raw vs billed tokens), (b) set expectations around caching and retries/fallbacks, and (c) document the dispute/credits process in a way that matches Finance/Legal policy.

Context: We’ve had multiple support threads where invoice token counts did not match what customers inferred from client-side tokenizers or from older doc language, plus confusion around streaming disconnects and retry behavior. In parallel, Engineering is rolling out metering fixes (idempotency/dedupe, cache-hit attribution, OpenAI-compat alignment) behind shadow-billing. This doc update is meant to be stable and accurate both before and after the meter fixes, while clearly calling out what can change.

What changed (high level): 1) Added an explicit “Raw tokens vs billed tokens” section with definitions and examples. 2) Clarified caching semantics: cache hits can reduce billed tokens; customers will see cache hit attribution in usage where available. 3) Clarified retries/fallbacks: Redwood does not intentionally double-bill retries; how we dedupe is described at a behavior level (not implementation details). 4) Streaming: added guidance on partial generations, disconnects, and what counts as “generated” for billing; wording avoids promising per-chunk determinism and focuses on billed token reporting as source of truth. 5) Dispute process: added a plain-language dispute window and required artifacts (request IDs, date range, export) and linked to support escalation path; explicitly states that credits/refunds are reviewed case-by-case under contract terms.

Notes on wording choices: This PR intentionally avoids tying the definition of billed tokens to a specific tokenizer library name/version. Instead, it defines billed tokens as “the token counts reported by Redwood in usage exports/console for a request” and explains that these are computed server-side using the model’s tokenization rules and Redwood’s billing attribution rules (e.g., caching). Legal asked that we avoid language that can be read as a guarantee that ‘client token counts = invoice token counts.’

Follow-ups (out of scope): a) Once ENG exposes billed_tokens + cache_hit fields broadly in the customer usage API, we should add a screenshot + API example (blocked on rollout). b) Add a dedicated page for ‘Usage exports & timezone behavior’ once the export TZ fix lands; for now this PR adds a short note and points customers to UTC as the canonical boundary.

Internal references: Meter fixes / fields referenced in copy are being implemented in other repos (redwood PRs and SDK PRs). This PR is purely documentation and does not change billing behavior.
commits: docs: rewrite Usage & Billing FAQ structure and add glossary for token terms
docs: add caching + retries + streaming clarifications and examples
docs: add dispute process section + links to support and usage exports
docs: polish language per Legal review (avoid absolute guarantees; clarify definitions)
docs: add changelog note and redirect from legacy FAQ anchors
review_conversation: Soojin Lee (Product Marketing): The new ‘billed tokens’ definition reads a bit defensive. Can we add a short paragraph framing this as ‘for fairness and predictability, we show billed tokens per request’ and then give a concrete example? (Also would be good to mention cache hits can reduce billed tokens.)

Elliot Price (Author): Updated the intro paragraph and added a worked example under ‘Raw vs billed’ showing prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, billed_tokens with a cache-hit note. Also added a one-liner that the Console/usage export is the canonical record for billing.

Michael Grant (Legal): Two tweaks: (1) remove “we will not bill for failed retries” — too absolute; instead say we aim to avoid double-billing and investigate anomalies. (2) Dispute language: use ‘within the dispute window specified in your Order Form’ rather than stating a universal number of days.

Elliot Price (Author): Done. Replaced the absolute statement with behavior-level wording + ‘contact Support with request IDs’. Updated dispute section to reference Order Form/MSA terms and kept a generic ‘promptly’ suggestion. Added an explicit ‘contract governs’ sentence.

Nadia Rahman (Telemetry): In the streaming section, the line ‘we bill only for tokens delivered to the client’ is not always true if the connection drops after generation but before all chunks are delivered. Suggest we say we bill based on server-side generated tokens for the request, as reported in usage, and note that disconnects can lead to fewer tokens received than generated.

Elliot Price (Author): Adjusted streaming section accordingly and added a short FAQ entry: ‘Why did I receive fewer tokens than billed_tokens?’ with disconnect explanation + recommendation to use request_id for debugging.
Monica Patel (SDK): Please avoid implying the SDK retries are always enabled. Different clients can configure retries. Also, add that idempotency keys are recommended for safe client retries.

Elliot Price (Author): Updated retry section to note retries may be performed by client, gateway, or server depending on configuration and failure type, and added a small best-practice callout: set idempotency_key for safe client-side retries.
Chris Osei (Product Ops): Can we add a caveat for experiments / changing meters? Something like ‘if we update how usage is displayed, we’ll communicate and preserve auditability.’

Elliot Price (Author): Added a short ‘Meter and reporting changes’ note: we may add fields/clarify attribution; invoices are based on the billing ledger; usage exports are for transparency and reconciliation; material changes follow change-control.
release_notes: Docs: Clarified billed token definitions and how caching impacts billed usage.
Docs: Expanded guidance on retries, streaming disconnects, and request ID-based reconciliation.
Docs: Documented dispute/credits workflow and linked to usage export guidance.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Soojin Lee on 2026-02-22 after Legal + Telemetry approvals; branch deleted.
